title: Assertive Boundary Setting (DESC Model)
goal: Explore assertive Boundary Setting (DESC Model) at a comfortable, adaptable level.
readiness: Adolescent encounters complex social dynamics and peer expectations.
steps: Identify a scenario where peer expectations violate personal comfort, values, or safety.
Rehearse the 4-part DESC script: (D) Describe the situation objectively, (E) Express personal feelings without accusation, (S) Specify the requested boundary, (C) Clarify positive consequences.
Rehearse saying a firm 'No' with calm, direct eye contact and neutral vocal pitch without defensive over-explaining.
completionCriteria: Participant rehearses a boundary in a comfortable communication style without a required tone or eye contact.
safety: Affirm that setting healthy boundaries is a sign of self-respect and emotional maturity.
adaptations: Use shorter attempts, accessible materials or additional support.
Adapt the activity to your language, interests, health and current ability; participation does not require unassisted performance.
benefits: Offers voluntary practice with shared attention, connection and expressing preferences or feelings.

title: Adaptable Aerobic Intervals
goal: Explore adaptable Aerobic Intervals at a comfortable, adaptable level.
readiness: Adolescent completes 20+ minutes of continuous running or sport activity without issue.
steps: Choose a familiar enjoyable aerobic activity and start easily.
Increase effort only to a personally manageable pace; at moderate intensity you can talk but not sing.
Alternate activity and easy recovery as desired, then finish gradually; no fixed heart-rate zone is required.
completionCriteria: Participant completes a self-chosen interval of activity and recovery without symptoms; no heart-rate recovery cutoff is used.
safety: Stop for chest pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness and seek medical advice as appropriate.
Start with manageable amounts and build gradually; adapt to health conditions and professional advice.
adaptations: Use shorter attempts, accessible materials or additional support.
Adapt the activity to your language, interests, health and current ability; participation does not require unassisted performance.
benefits: Offers adaptable practice with movement or everyday hand skills. Choose support and effort that feel comfortable.

title: Hypothetico-Deductive Scientific Modeling
goal: Explore hypothetico-Deductive Scientific Modeling at a comfortable, adaptable level.
readiness: Adolescent handles multi-variable school science labs.
steps: Select a physical or biological system with multiple variables (e.g., pendulum period vs. string length, bob mass, and release angle).
Formulate an explicit hypothesis predicting the causal variable.
Conduct 5 trials altering ONLY the chosen independent variable while strictly standardizing all other parameters.
Graph collected data, calculate mean variances, and deduce a formal mathematical or qualitative rule.
completionCriteria: Produces a documented scientific lab report correctly isolating one causal variable, presenting plotted data, and deducing a verifiable conclusion.
safety: Ensure experimental materials are safe and supervised.
adaptations: Use shorter attempts, accessible materials or additional support.
Adapt the activity to your language, interests, health and current ability; participation does not require unassisted performance.
benefits: Offers practice with exploration, learning and problem solving at a personally suitable level.

title: Extemporaneous Public Rhetoric & Keynote Delivery
goal: Explore extemporaneous Public Rhetoric & Keynote Delivery at a comfortable, adaptable level.
readiness: Adolescent delivers prepared classroom oral presentations.
steps: Draw an unfamiliar contemporary topic prompt from a selection.
Take exactly 3 minutes to outline an index card with: Hook, Point 1 (Problem), Point 2 (Evidence), Point 3 (Solution), Call to Action.
Stand before an audience or camera and deliver the speech for 3 full minutes without reading verbatim.
Focus on maintaining open posture, projecting from the diaphragm, and replacing vocal fillers ('um', 'like') with purposeful pauses.
completionCriteria: Participant practises conveying a main idea to a chosen audience using notes or accessible communication.
safety: Maintain an encouraging, supportive audience environment.
adaptations: Use shorter attempts, accessible materials or additional support.

title: Scenario-Based Risk vs. Reward Deconstruction
goal: Explore scenario-Based Risk vs. Reward Deconstruction at a comfortable, adaptable level.
reps: Optional planning example: 2 days per week; adapt or skip as needed.
duration: Up to 15 minutes per planned opportunity, with breaks or shorter attempts as needed.
imagePrompt: A 15-year-old sitting at a desk with an adult mentor, reviewing scenario decision cards analyzing short-term impulses versus long-term outcomes.
benefits: Offers practice with exploration, learning and problem solving at a personally suitable level.
completionCriteria: Adolescent articulates both the short-term emotional driver and long-term consequence for 3 distinct scenarios, demonstrating a rehearsed exit script for each.
steps: Review 3 realistic high-arousal scenarios (e.g., passenger in a speeding vehicle, unvetted online dares, party substance pressure).
Deconstruct the scenario using a dual-column analysis: 'Immediate Limbic Payoff' (peer approval, thrill) versus 'Long-Term Structural Risk' (injury, legal, relational).
Identify personal physiological warning signs of impulsive arousal (accelerated heart rate, tunnel vision).
Script and rehearse an immediate, face-saving exit strategy.
